summary: Master project management tailored for community development. Enroll in our training to gain essential skills and knowledge for successful community initiatives
lede: Project management skills for community development help turn development goals, community priorities, and field activities into a workable delivery system. You will learn to structure needs assessments, participation, activity sequencing, resources, risks, indicators, outcomes, and verification sources using the Logical Framework Approach, Theory of Change, Results-Based Management, and selected OECD DAC evaluation criteria. Through practical planning and monitoring exercises, you will create project documents including a charter, stakeholder map, work breakdown structure, budget tracker, risk register, RACI matrix, schedule, monitoring plan, and reporting concept. The course also introduces adaptive management, responsible digital data use, Sphere Handbook and Core Humanitarian Standard principles, and AI-assisted analysis at an overview level.
audienceIntro: This foundation-to-intermediate course is designed for professionals who coordinate, support, monitor, or govern international community development projects and need practical control over delivery and results.
modules: Theory of Change and Logical Frameworks
prerequisites: No formal project management certification is required. You should have basic experience supporting community programmes, development activities, nonprofit operations, grants, monitoring, or partner coordination. Coding is not required, and you do not need prior experience with Microsoft Project or Power BI. Advanced digital analysis is taught at conceptual and operational application level, while planning, monitoring, risk, and reporting exercises receive hands-on practice.
